records.name: Philadelphia Trail Club
records.summary: A nonprofit hiking club founded in 1931 that leads hikes most weekends in Philadelphia and nearby counties. Anyone can join the free public hikes, and members can grow into hike leaders.
records.what_you_do: Walk 5 to 10 mile hikes, each with a difficulty rating, and take part in the club's member trips. The yearly member trip is usually one major trip and has gone abroad and to other states.

schedule.text: Hikes most weekends, less often in July and August

cost.text: Membership is $10 a year. Public hikes are free.

first_step.how: Go on a free public hike from the club's hike list. To join, apply online or by mail with a signed waiver and $10 dues.
first_step.basis: Non-members can take public hikes and each hike has a difficulty rating, but the site does not describe a welcome for first-timers.

records.notes: The club's public hikes listing would not load, so no upcoming hike dates are recorded. A June 2025 article says the club is 94 years old and skews middle-aged and older; the crowd tag reflects that.

records.name: Appalachian Mountain Club, Delaware Valley Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia-area chapter of the national Appalachian Mountain Club. It runs hikes, paddling trips, bike rides, and camping outings, and its volunteers look after local trails and conservation work.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for an outing from the chapter calendar, volunteer for trail work or conservation, or train toward leading trips yourself. The chapter says it hosts more than 800 outings a year and that most activities are free.

schedule.text: More than 800 outings a year, listed on the chapter's activities calendar

locations.label: Outings across greater Philadelphia and nearby counties

cost.text: Most activities are free, per the chapter. Check each outing for details.

first_step.how: Pick an outing on the chapter's activities calendar and sign up. The site links a membership page, but does not say whether each outing needs one.
first_step.basis: The public calendar and a contact page give a clear way in, but the site does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: The home page lists no dated outings. Two points came from search summaries that we did not open on a page, so they are not recorded: a rule that under-18s must be with a parent at Pennsylvania chapter events, and a 20s and 30s trip series. Check both on the chapter calendar before using them.

records.name: Philadelphia Grotto
records.summary: A caving club chartered in 1947 as a chapter of the National Speleological Society. Members explore caves, protect them, and help newcomers learn to cave with experienced leaders.
records.what_you_do: Go on caving trips led by experienced members, take part in cave conservation and education, and come to the monthly meeting to get a membership form. Wear layers of synthetic insulating clothing, since caves sit near 55 degrees and are very humid.

schedule.text: Meets the first Thursday of each month, hosted at a member's home in Media, PA and online

locations.label: Member's home in Media, PA (address is on the club's meeting page)

cost.text: Not stated on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Attend a first-Thursday meeting, in person or online. The club hands out its membership form there, and beginners cave with experienced leaders.
first_step.basis: The site names a clear first step (come to a meeting for the membership form) and gives advice written for beginners, but it does not describe any training.

records.notes: The meeting pages give no year, so no dated evidence is recorded. Age rules, dues and the first-trip steps are not on the pages read. The site's New Cavers link goes to the new-members page, which was read. Member names on the meeting page were left out.

records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: A paddling club founded in 1905 that teaches kayaking, canoeing, and paddleboarding and runs trips through the year from its grounds in Fairmount Park. Its lessons, trips, and events are open to people who are not members.
records.what_you_do: Take a paddling lesson, join a river trip, or come to a work day on the grounds. The club also trains people toward whitewater and racing, and it holds a monthly club meeting.

schedule.text: Monthly club meetings at 7:30 pm, with lessons, trips, and work days through the year. Listed 2026 dates include a fall work day on 10 Oct 2026 at 9:30 am.

cost.text: Lesson and trip prices were not found. Full membership: a $25 application fee plus dues up to $180 a year, per a June 2025 Inquirer article.

first_step.how: Sign up for a lesson or a public trip through the club's site. Full membership needs an application and sponsorship by a current member.
first_step.basis: The club says it trains new paddlers, and its trips and events are open to people who are not members.

records.notes: The club's home page lists no dues, so the membership cost comes from the June 2025 article. The article says joining requires sponsorship; the club's own site says trips need no membership. Both are shown.

records.name: Delaware Valley Amateur Astronomers
records.summary: An amateur astronomy club serving the Philadelphia area since 1976. It runs public star parties and holds free monthly meetings where anyone can learn about the night sky.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free monthly meeting, then join a Star Watch or dark-sky star party to look at the sky. The club also runs telescope-making workshops, lectures, and clinics.

schedule.text: Free monthly meetings, usually on Friday evenings. Star Watch nights listed for fall 2026: Sat Oct 17, 7 to 9 pm (no location listed), and Sat Nov 14, 4:30 to 9:30 pm at Valley Forge.

locations.label: Monthly meetings, Radnor Township Building, Radnorshire Room
Star Watch nights, Valley Forge National Historical Park, Model Airplane Field

cost.text: Monthly meetings are free and open to the public. The listing does not say whether Star Watch nights cost money.

first_step.how: Come to a free monthly meeting or a Star Watch night. The club's site has a contact form for questions.
first_step.basis: Meetings are free and public and star parties are open, but the listing does not describe beginner classes or a joining process.

records.notes: The club's own site (dvaa.org) returned HTTP 403 to our reader, so every fact here comes from the NASA Night Sky Network club listing, a public listing. Re-check the club site when it is reachable. The listing shows a contact person, and that person is not recorded.

records.name: Latino Outdoors Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia part of Latino Outdoors, a group that gets Latine people outside for hikes, paddling, and other outdoor activities. Its local team hosts monthly outings around the city and across the state.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly outing, such as the kayaking day at FDR Park that the group ran with a partner in June 2025. Sign up for the community email list to hear about the next trip.

locations.label: Outings around Philadelphia and across Pennsylvania (places vary), including FDR Park

first_step.how: Join the group's community email list (linked from its site) and watch its Outings and Events page for the next Philadelphia trip.
first_step.basis: The site links a community list and an outings page, but neither the site nor the 2025 article explains a first-outing process.

records.notes: The group's home page does not mention Philadelphia. The people page lists a Philadelphia outings leader and a Philadelphia program coordinator; their names are not recorded. The June 2025 article is the only dated item. The community listserv link comes from the site's navigation. The people page is long, and we read two parts of it.

records.name: Philly Hiking Beauties
records.summary: A nonprofit women's hiking group focused on health and friendship. It leads weekly hikes, fitness challenges, social events, and trips, and it helps with road cleanups.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a hike on the group's events calendar, join a fitness challenge or social event, or help with a cleanup. The group also runs a summer outdoor program for girls in the Delaware County area.

schedule.text: Weekly hikes, listed on the group's Calendar of Events

first_step.how: Open the Calendar of Events on the group's site and sign up for a hike. The Join Us menu item leads to the contact page.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear way to find hikes and make contact, but does not describe what a first hike is like.

records.notes: The homepage shows no dated hikes. Its photo captions mention the Schuylkill River Trail, Great Falls, and Yosemite, but none are dated. The Little Hiking Beauties page gives a May 9 start and a 7 week run with no year and no age range; the sign-up form did not show in the text we read. The City Cast Philly page gives ages 5 to 12, but that is not from the group's own site, so it is not recorded.

records.name: HIKE+HEAL
records.summary: A women's hiking community focused on wellness and friendship outdoors. It offers healing hikes, after-work Happy Hour Hikes, wellness events, and field trips, and it welcomes women of all fitness levels.
records.what_you_do: Join a healing hike or a weekday Happy Hour Hike, which ends with drinks from local juice makers. The group also runs field trips, wellness events, and retreats.

schedule.text: Healing hikes, weekday Happy Hour Hikes after work, and other events, listed on the group's upcoming events page

cost.text: Membership price is not shown on the group's site. Event prices are not shown on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Sign up for the next hike on the group's upcoming events page, which the site links as 'Join our next hike'. A newsletter sign-up is also on the site.
first_step.basis: The site says women of all fitness levels are welcome and links straight to the next hike, but it does not describe what a first hike is like.

records.notes: The site shows no dates. A City Cast Philly page without a year lists a $350 yearly membership and some free community hikes. Neither is confirmed on the group's site, so neither is recorded. Its events run through a lu.ma calendar that we did not read.

records.name: BATONA Hiking Club of Philadelphia
records.summary: A long-running hiking club that goes on short and long hikes in Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, and New Jersey. Members carpool to trailheads, and experienced leaders run the hikes.
records.what_you_do: Join a short or long hike from the club's Meetup calendar, carpool with other members, and hike at the group's pace.

schedule.text: Weekend hikes, short and long, listed on the club's Meetup calendar

cost.text: About $3 a year plus $1 per hike, per a June 2025 Inquirer article.

first_step.how: Join the club's Meetup group and sign up for a hike listed there.
first_step.basis: Joining is open through a public Meetup page, and the 2025 article describes led hikes, but the club's own site could not be read.

records.notes: The club's own site (batona.org) returned an empty page twice, so the facts come from a June 2025 Inquirer article and a City Cast Philly page. The article says the club is 96 years old with about 170 members. The article also says the Outdoor Club of South Jersey now maintains the 53-mile Batona Trail. Re-check the site and the Meetup calendar before publishing.

records.name: Outdoor Club of South Jersey
records.notes: Based in South Jersey (mailing address in Oceanville, NJ). Membership requires dues, and trips run through Meetup groups. The site does not say it serves Philadelphia city residents. A June 2025 article lists it among Philadelphia-area clubs, which is why it was checked.

records.name: Delaware Astronomical Society
records.notes: A Delaware club. Its site points to Delaware places such as the Sawin Observatory and does not mention Philadelphia. Its monthly meetings are open to the public. Recorded so it is not re-found as a Philadelphia group.

leads_only.name: Body Liberation Outdoor Club, Greater Philadelphia chapter
leads_only.note: Named in a City Cast Philly list as the Philly chapter. Instagram only, not verified. The national site (bodyliberationoutdoorclub.org) was read and does not name a Philly chapter.

leads_only.name: Black Girls Hike Philly
leads_only.note: Named in a City Cast Philly list. Instagram only, no own website identified. Serves Black women with hikes, trail runs and meetups.

leads_only.name: OUT on the Trails
leads_only.note: Queer-centered outdoor group, a subgroup of Sip City Mixer per City Cast Philly. Free seasonal hikes, plus rock climbing and bird watching. Instagram only, no own website identified.

leads_only.name: Philly Trail Wanderers
leads_only.note: Meetup group surfaced in search results. Lead only, not read.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Hiking and Adventure Group
leads_only.note: Named in an undated Philadelphia Magazine article, which describes weekend hikes arranged by email. No own website identified. Lead only.

blocked.note: Delaware Valley Amateur Astronomers own site. Forbidden to our reader. The NASA club listing gives the site as dvaa.org; the record relies on that listing.
BATONA own site returned an empty page on two tries, with and without www. Not readable.
Philadelphia Trail Club public hikes listing did not load (CSS error page). Not readable.

notes: Budget: all 3 WebSearch calls used; 35 WebFetch calls used, well under the 60 cap. Covered with a record: Philadelphia Trail Club, AMC Delaware Valley Chapter, Philadelphia Grotto, Philadelphia Canoe Club, Delaware Valley Amateur Astronomers, Latino Outdoors Philadelphia, Philly Hiking Beauties, HIKE+HEAL, BATONA (from a 2025 article, own site unreadable), plus two out of area clubs (Outdoor Club of South Jersey, Delaware Astronomical Society). NOT COVERED, budget ran out: (1) Outdoor Afro Philadelphia: outdoorafro.com home, /philadelphia, /locations and /our-locations gave no Philadelphia chapter (404s or no Philly content), and no search was left to find it. (2) Delaware Valley geocaching groups: not searched at all. (3) Climbing community groups: no dedicated Philly climbing group found; climbing appears only in the OUT on the Trails and Latino Outdoors entries. (4) Camping and backpacking: covered through Philadelphia Trail Club, AMC DV and BATONA; no separate camping club found. A later search could cover geocaching, climbing and Outdoor Afro. Dropped with reasons: Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia (cycling advocacy, belongs to another lane); Discovery Pathways (partner organization, not a club); Franklin Institute Joel N. Bloom Observatory and Drexel Joseph R. Lynch Observatory public nights (venues, not groups); Wissahickon Trails star party event (park friends group, another lane). Wrong or missing URLs: phillytrailclub.org did not resolve; dvas.org is a Vermont Deaf advocacy group, not an astronomy club. No Meetup page was read in depth. Facts from search summaries that were not checked on a page are left out. Date to watch: the Philadelphia Canoe Club fall work day is 10 Oct 2026, two days after today.
